title: Keep hard-failing finalists behind viable finalists even if their raw total is higher

problem_spec.request: Find the best retention strategy for a workflow-heavy B2B product that wants a stronger moat without becoming enterprise-only.
constraints: Stay self-serve for teams under 50 seats.
Keep every recommendation auditable from stored artifacts.
success_criteria: Increase repeated weekly use by team leads.
Create a retention mechanism that gets stronger as real work accumulates.

candidate.thesis: Workflow-native decision archive with guided onboarding
candidate.mechanism: Preserve every serious decision branch, attach reusable playbooks to those artifacts, and preload the first ritual so teams feel retained value before deep configuration.
assumptions: Teams will accept light workflow setup if the artifact value appears immediately.
strengths: Balances moat strength with easier activation.
unknowns: Which ritual best demonstrates retained value in week one?
candidate.implementation_shape: Launch with one preloaded weekly ritual and expand after usage proves out.
evidence: The brief rewards retained workflow value and self-serve adoption.

candidate.thesis: Workflow-native decision archive with benchmark layer
candidate.mechanism: Start from the retained decision archive, then add trusted peer benchmarks once enough internal workflow data exists to support credible comparisons.
assumptions: Teams will share benchmark data after the private archive already proves value.
strengths: Raises the upside ceiling beyond the private archive alone.
failure_modes: Adds more trust and sequencing risk.
unknowns: How quickly can benchmark participation become credible?
candidate.implementation_shape: Private archive first, benchmark cohort second.
evidence: The brief allows bold extensions if the tradeoffs remain explicit.

candidate.mechanism: Convert strong decisions into auditable checklists embedded in one recurring team workflow, then expand only if the retained checklist artifacts change behavior.
assumptions: Teams will adopt a narrower workflow wedge if it saves recurring coordination time.
strengths: Very tractable and easy to trial.
failure_modes: Could create a weaker moat than archive-centric approaches.
unknowns: Will the narrow wedge feel differentiated enough?
candidate.implementation_shape: Launch in one workflow first and measure repeated use.
evidence: The brief values auditable artifacts and retained workflow habits.

candidate.mechanism: Use a dedicated strategist to configure each account, hand-build reports, and manually run the retention ritual for them.
assumptions: High-touch services can substitute for product retention in the early market.
strengths: Could show strong results for a few accounts quickly.
unknowns: Can any product value survive after the services layer is removed?
candidate.implementation_shape: Start with a consulting-heavy customer-success motion.
evidence: Services may improve retention for some accounts, but not within the actual brief.

hard_constraint_reasons: Depends on a services-heavy rollout instead of self-serve adoption.
Produces bespoke human outputs instead of auditable product artifacts.
